_doc: Shipped defaults for email_drafts.json -- the draft_email tool (email_drafts.py). Edit email_drafts.json, not this file; any key missing or invalid there falls back to the value here, with a log line. Denisse never sends: every backend below only SAVES a draft, and he presses Send. Paths starting with ~ are under his home folder. Templates are str.format strings and may only use the {fields} their default here uses.

backends._doc: Tried in this order; the first that saves wins. outlook_desktop: classic Outlook's COM object (Outlook.Application) -- the draft is saved into his Drafts folder, never sent; absent on this machine on 2026-11-07 (only the new Outlook app, which has no local automation). eml_file: a .eml file in drafts_folder that Outlook opens as an unsent message, plus the text on the clipboard.

eml._doc: drafts_folder: where .eml drafts go. extra_headers: X-Unsent makes classic Outlook open the file as an unsent draft with a Send button. file_name: {date} is today (date_format), {subject} the subject with unsafe characters dropped and cut to max_name_chars.

clipboard._doc: The draft's text goes on the clipboard too, so he can paste it into any mail app. command gets the text on stdin in encoding (utf-16 carries a BOM, which clip.exe reads as Unicode).

recipients._doc: Who a draft is to comes from what he said (an address, or a name in contacts_file) or from the email being replied to (reply_headers, first found wins). Never guessed: anything else is a question back to him. contacts_file: private, [{"name": ..., "address": ..., "aliases": [...]}]; a name matches when its words equal his words once filler_words are dropped.

attachments._doc: Files named in plain words ('my latest CV'). Each kind: words -- any of these in his phrase picks this kind; folder -- where its files live; patterns -- file names that count (first pattern with a match wins); recursive -- look in subfolders too. The newest matching file is used. A phrase that is an existing full path is attached as it is. Nothing else is guessed.

writing._doc: How the body is written: the local chat model (config.json models.chat), given voice + his saved reply preferences (reply_preferences.py) + the request. reply_prefix: added to the original subject for a reply. sign_off: appended when the body doesn't already end with his name.
writing.name: Chuen
voice: You write emails for Chuen, a university student, in his own voice, as if he typed them himself.
Humble, polite and plain. Short sentences. British spelling.
Say only what his gist says. Never add claims about him, his work or his plans that the gist doesn't give.
No AI tells: no 'I hope this email finds you well', no 'delve', no 'I am writing to', no bullet lists, no em dashes, no exclamation marks.
Write only the body: the greeting, a few short paragraphs, nothing after the last sentence. No subject line, no sign-off, no notes to Chuen.

wording._doc: What the tool tells her. 'Error: ' / 'Refused' openings are read by brain.py as no evidence that anything happened.
wording.ready: Draft ready -- {where}.{clipboard} To: {to}. Subject: {subject}. Attached: {attachments}. Nothing was sent. Tell him it's ready and that he presses Send himself.
wording.on_clipboard: The text is on your clipboard too.
wording.ask_recipient: Refused: no draft made. I can't tell who this goes to{detail}. Ask him, in one short question, for their email address. Never guess one.
wording.ask_recipient_detail: -- '{value}' isn't an address or a saved contact
wording.ask_recipient_ambiguous: Refused: no draft made. '{value}' could be {options}. Ask him which one, in one short question.
wording.ask_subject: Refused: no draft made -- there's no subject. Ask him what the email is about in a few words, or pass a short subject yourself.
wording.ask_gist: Refused: no draft made -- nothing says what the email should say. Ask him what he wants to tell them.
wording.ask_attachment: Refused: no draft made. I don't know which file '{value}' is. Ask him which file he means, or use find_files and pass its full path.
wording.missing_attachment: Refused: no draft made. There's no {kind} in {folder} ({patterns}). Tell him, and ask which file to attach.
wording.folder_not_set: Refused: no draft made. No folder is set for his {kind} (email_drafts.json attachments). Tell him, and ask which file to attach.
wording.writer_failed: Error: couldn't write the email ({error}). No draft was made.
wording.save_failed: Error: couldn't save the draft anywhere ({error}). Nothing was sent.
